stem: A food manufacturing study measures the weight (grams) for a sample of 25 cereal boxes. The sample mean is 590.3 g with a sample standard deviation of 59.0 g. However, 3 of the 25 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 22 observations have a mean of 569.9 g and standard deviation of 42.2 g. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 590.3, 95% CI = [565.9, 614.7]. Without outliers: mean = 569.9, 95% CI = [551.9, 587.9]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [551.9, 614.7]. Point estimate: 580.1 g.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [551.9, 614.7].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
